clue.text: Cold — remains only to get material

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
ash is what remains after burning
mere means only or nothing more than

explanation.surface: A grim instruction: with someone gone cold and only their ashes left, go and buy fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine soft wool from goats, used as a cloth, is a material.

clue.text: Politeness ensures order in a large town

indicators.note: in tells us the order is placed inside the town

parts.note: a city is a large town
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Good manners keep a big town running in an orderly way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ensures' is just a link; the Order of Merit is a British honour, and 'in' sets it within the large town.
explanation.definitionFit: Comity is courtesy and mutual civility, especially between nations.

clue.text: Dreads becoming more melancholy

indicators.note: becoming signals that the letters of the previous word turn into something new

explanation.surface: Someone who dreads things grows gloomier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges the letters of DREADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of sad: gloomier, more sorrowful.

clue.text: A little drummer many consider a fabulous guy

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small percussionist whom many regard as a legend.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'consider', a verb, which cannot stand for a noun; 'consider' is a link and the definition is 'a fabulous guy', fabulous meaning from fable.
explanation.definitionFit: A male sea-creature of folklore, the counterpart of a mermaid, is a guy of fable.

clue.text: "..the olive grove of Academe Plato's Milton" (Paradise Regained)

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads "..the olive grove of Academe Plato's Milton" (Paradise Regained): a fill-in quotation whose blank is garbled by OCR, with 'Milton' sitting inside the quote where the missing word belongs; no wordplay to annotate.
annotationWithheld.clue: "..the olive grove of Academe Plato's Milton" (Paradise Regained)

clue.text: Some songstresses feel the pressure

indicators.note: Some tells us only part of the next word is taken, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Female singers feeling the strain before a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' points at a run of letters inside SONGSTRESSES; 'feel the' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is strain or force pressing on something, or on a person.

clue.text: Cross note about people leading a wild life

indicators.note: about says the note wraps round the people that follow

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
ravers are party-goers living it up

explanation.surface: An irritated remark about hedonists who live wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective (angry) but is the verb; 'about' wraps the sol-fa note round the party-goers.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across or go over something.

clue.text: Blissful area of London still

parts.note: EC is the postcode district of the City of London
static means motionless, still

explanation.surface: A part of London that is wonderfully peaceful.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is a London postcode area (East Central, the City).
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overjoyed, in a state of rapture.

clue.text: Acting as guide, always in smart surroundings

indicators.note: in places the word for always within another
surroundings says the word for smart encloses the other piece

parts.note: to smart is to sting
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A guide who is always well turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' looks like an adjective (well dressed) but is the verb sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Steering is directing the course of something, guiding it.

clue.text: Middle-of-the-road tome read for a change

indicators.note: for a change says the letters of the two words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone choosing an unexciting book to read for variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges TOME and READ.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate views avoid extremes, which is what middle-of-the-road means.

clue.text: Dance to look on as old hat

parts.note: pas is a ballet step or dance
to see is to look on, watch

explanation.surface: Going to watch a dance that seems dated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link. PAS is the French ballet term for a step.
explanation.definitionFit: Passé describes something out of fashion, outdated.

clue.text: Their use might well result in words being exchanged!

definitions.text: Their use might well result in words being exchanged!

parts.words: Their use might well result in words being exchanged!
parts.note: words being exchanged looks like an argument, but it means swapping one word for another of the same meaning using reference books of synonyms

explanation.surface: Something that tends to provoke a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'words being exchanged' suggests a quarrel; the books are lists of synonyms, used to replace one word with another.
explanation.definitionFit: Books listing synonyms let a writer exchange one word for another.

clue.text: Look after stuff-maintain in good order

indicators.note: after says the look comes behind the stuff in the answer

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric, a stuff
an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: Looking after things and keeping them in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as one phrase meaning care for, but 'after' simply places the look behind the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair something is to fix and keep it in working condition.

clue.text: It's no train conversion

indicators.note: conversion signals that the letters of the preceding words are converted into a new order

parts.note: it's is it is, giving its letters as written

explanation.surface: A rail vehicle that has been refitted as something other than a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' rearranges ITSNOTRAIN; the whole clue also defines, since a conversion is a change of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A transition is a change from one state to another, as a conversion is.

clue.text: A vague idea permission could be given

indicators.note: could be given suggests the letters of the word before can be handed out in another order

explanation.surface: Someone hopes they may be granted consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be given' rearranges PERMISSION.
explanation.definitionFit: An impression is a hazy notion or feeling about something.

clue.text: Box is to be put in run

indicators.note: to be put in says the word is goes inside the run

parts.note: a canter is a gentle run, as of a horse

explanation.surface: Instructions for packing a box into a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like the sport or verb but is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a small container, a box or tin.

clue.text: Sizes up silly females?

definitions.meaning: to size up is to evaluate
silly creatures are asses; add the feminine ending -ess and pluralise, as with lioness

explanation.surface: Someone judging women unkindly as foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: female asses (fools), built like 'lionesses', hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Evaluates and judges, and also a jokey plural of a female fool.

clue.text: They have a yen for spending

definitions.text: They have a yen for spending

parts.words: They have a yen for spending
parts.note: a yen for spending reads as a longing to shop, but the yen is a currency, which a certain nation's people use to spend

explanation.surface: Shopaholics who love to splash out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' is a craving and also the currency of Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of the nation whose money is the yen spend in yen.

clue.text: Teetotal seaman making his mark?

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
staining is leaving a mark on something

explanation.surface: A sailor who doesn't drink, signing his name.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is the usual crossword abbreviation for able seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abstaining from alcohol is teetotal.

clue.text: See about article about society meeting

indicators.note: the first about says the word see goes round the following pieces

parts.note: taken as written
an is the indefinite article
c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A request to look into an article concerning a society gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'about's do different jobs: the first is the container signal, the second gives C (circa).
explanation.definitionFit: A séance is a session of a society; nowadays chiefly one trying to contact spirits.

clue.text: Hurt-drink more than really necessary

parts.note: to mar is to damage or hurt
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Drinking more than one needs and getting hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is an extra allowance beyond what is strictly required.

clue.text: Intellectual man let loose

indicators.note: let loose suggests the letters are set free to reorder

explanation.surface: A clever man being released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges MAN and LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental relates to the mind, as intellectual does.

clue.text: A high-brow being in charge, step back

indicators.note: back says the word for step is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a pace is a step

explanation.surface: An intellectual in authority being made to step down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-brow' suggests an intellectual, but it is the brow of a high mountain. 'back' turns PACE into ECAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent covering of ice sits on a high summit or brow.

clue.text: It could be a tribe held by the French will be set free

indicators.note: held by says the scrambled letters sit within the French word

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: It could be signals that the letters of the following words can take another form

explanation.surface: A tribe imprisoned by the French will be released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It could be' rearranges A TRIBE into IBERAT, and 'held by' places that inside the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate is to free from captivity.

clue.text: A canopy to check with a certain hesitation

parts.note: to test is to check
er is the sound of a hesitation

explanation.surface: Inspecting a canopy somewhat uncertainly.
explanation.walkthrough: A tester is the canopy over a four-poster bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester is a canopy over a bed or pulpit.

clue.text: Day's ending

parts.note: the moment a day finishes at twelve o'clock at night, not merely evening or dusk

explanation.definitionFit: Twelve at night is when one day ends and the next begins.

clue.text: Somewhat less prudent when there's tasty food!

explanation.surface: Getting reckless when good food is on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when there's' links the two meanings: more rash, and a slice of bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: More reckless, and also a thin slice of bacon or ham.

clue.text: Draw a quarter-almost all find this outrageous

parts.note: to infer is to draw a conclusion
N, north, is a compass quarter

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the word all is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone sketching a district finds it scandalous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests sketching but means deduce. 'almost' cuts ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal means hellish, and colloquially outrageous or detestable.
